correctness.rationale: For any n, two-term weakly prime-additive representations are impossible: reduction mod one base p in p^a+q^b=n with p|n implies p|q^b. Independently enumerated exact integer factorizations and every positive power for all n≤8610 and every 4-subset of distinct prime divisors; the only 4-term candidate up to 8610 is 8610, with no 3-term representation and one 4-term witness (3,5,7,41) with powers (3⁸=6561,5²=25,7³=343,41²=1681). The exhaustive finite cutoff fully proves the least element; it does not claim density or infinitude. The pinned verify.py independently reconstructs the same complete search with a smallest-prime-factor sieve and exact Cartesian products.

originality.rationale: Leung’s length-4 paper proves (subject to prime existence/GRH) infinitude of length-four numbers divisible by any m but no least such value; searched complete primary PDF for 8610 with no match. OEIS A296717 lists 8610 as weakly prime-additive and nonshortest but also several earlier nonshortest values; that alone entails neither exact κ=4 nor its least position, nor unique four-term representation. The finite exhaustive search adds information not present in the database; unindexed brute-force precedent remains a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed computational note or database may already contain exact κ4 minimality for 8610.
Exhaustive cutoff 8610 has no implications for later class density or infinitude.

value.rationale: The first exact length-four element of a published arithmetic class is a natural sharp finite invariant, not an arbitrary bounded slice. A complete exact search identifies the first boundary and its unique witness, furnishing an unconditional computational benchmark for a class whose general infinitude has conditional proofs.
